$comment: Answers one question: can this door be afforded on this workload? It reads the latency percentile, the price of a decision, and the share of the workload the door declines. It reads no accuracy and no probabilities, because decision-v1 and probability-v1 already do, and neither of them judges time or money.

The gap this gate closes is measured. On the same 52-item suite, hosted Jev answers in about 250 ms, kev-0.5b in about 180, kev-4b in about a second, and Lev in about 2,100 ms, because Lev draws eight samples across four helpers and the isolation rule makes each draw pay the state cost. docs/lev/disposition.md ranks those four doors on accuracy, ECE, Brier, log loss, and confident errors, and nothing in that ranking would refuse a door that wins two points of accuracy and costs 1.4 seconds a turn. For a router in front of every agent turn, that door is the worse door.

No ceiling is stored here, and that is the design rather than an omission. A batch job tolerates 1.6 seconds and a router does not, so any universal latency constant is wrong for one of them whatever number it carries. The ceilings arrive with the measurement, in a Budget the caller states and names, and a criterion whose ceiling was not stated reports unverifiable rather than passed.

Cost has one rule of its own: a lane with no meter on it is recorded as unmetered_local_lane and never as a zero. Our own hardware still costs device time and power; what it lacks is a meter, not a price. A gate reading a zero there would admit a door on a price nobody quoted, which is the same fault as reading an unmeasured metric as zero.

Latency's own noise floor is not measured, so latency cannot refuse anything yet. docs/gym/measurements/2026-09-19-latency-noise-floor.md records the attempt and why it does not count: the machine was running nine agents against several copies of the same on-device model, one block's p95 came back at four times its neighbours', and the median drifted upward across every block of the sweep. That is a measurement of the contention. Recording it as this gate's floor would bake a busy afternoon into a digest, so latency_block_sigma_relative stays unmeasured and pending_measurement says what would fill it.
question: Can this door be afforded on this workload, in time and in money?

min_calls.why: By nearest rank, the 95th percentile of n calls is the call at position ceil(0.95 * n), which is n itself for every n below 20. A gate reading fewer than 20 timed calls is reading the slowest call of the run and calling it a percentile, and the slowest call of a short run is whatever the machine was doing at the time.

latency_block_sigma_relative.why: Nothing has measured how much a latency percentile moves between blocks of the same workload on the same machine with the same door. The sweep that tried is in docs/gym/measurements/2026-09-19-latency-noise-floor.md, and it measured a contended machine rather than a door: nine agents were running, one block's p95 was four times its neighbours', and the median rose in every block of the sweep. Until an uncontended sweep exists, every latency criterion reports unverifiable and no door is refused on a clock.

regression_sigmas.why: Two standard deviations is the conventional bar for calling a difference real. It is a convention and it is labelled one; the quantity it multiplies is the measurement. It scales the block-to-block latency spread, which is unmeasured, and the binomial standard error of a stated refusal ceiling, which is computed per comparison from the ceiling and the number of calls.

pending_measurement.quantity: the block-to-block spread of a latency percentile on an uncontended machine
pending_measurement.why: Run `gym latency` with the door, the items, and the item order held fixed, over at least eight blocks, on a machine running nothing else, and derive latency_block_sigma_relative from the p95 column. The measurement also has to say whether one relative spread transfers between a 180 ms door and a 1,600 ms door, because this rule applies one figure to both and would be substituting if it did not.
